questions.question: When inspecting a coupling under the trailer, you should:

options.text: Detach the jaws from around the kingpin.
Make sure the locking lever is in the "emergency" position.
Look into the back of the fifth wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look into the back of the fifth wheel.
questions.explanation: When inspecting a coupling under the trailer, look into the back of the fifth wheel. Make sure the fifth wheel jaws are locked around the kingpin.

questions.question: To test ____, move forward slowly and apply the brakes with the hand control.
questions.explanation: To test trailer service brakes, first check that air pressure is normal and release the parking brake. Then move forward slowly and apply the hand control. The trailer brakes should activate if they are working properly.

questions.question: A trailer that is too high:
questions.explanation: Before coupling a tractor and trailer, the trailer must be at the correct height. A trailer that is too low can damage the nose. A trailer that is too high may not couple correctly.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The trailer service air line is also called the control line or signal line.

questions.question: When driving with trailers, you should:

options.text: Make sudden turns with the steering wheel.
Push the accelerator to the floor when starting from a stop.

questions.explanation: Always steer gently and smoothly when pulling a trailer. Sudden steering moves can cause the trailer to tip over.

questions.question: The trailer hand valve should be used:

options.text: Only to test the trailer brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only to test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The trailer hand valve (also called the trolley valve or Johnson bar) controls the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while moving could cause a skid.

questions.question: What is a tractor protection valve?

options.text: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
A valve that prevents the truck from being stolen
A valve that prevents the driver from going too fast
A valve that prevents the trailer from accidentally being released

questions.correctAnswerText: A valve that keeps air in the brake system if there is a bad leak
questions.explanation: In a combination vehicle with air brakes, the tractor protection valve keeps air in the tractor or truck brake system if the trailer breaks away or develops a leak.

questions.question: During a trip, which shut-off valves should be open?

options.text: All shut-off valves should be open.
The rear shut-off valves should be open.
All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves.
No shut-off valves should be open.

questions.correctAnswerText: All shut-off valves should be open, except the rear shut-off valves.
questions.explanation: At the start of a trip, open all shut-off valves except the rear trailer shut-off valves. This ensures air reaches all trailer brakes and prevents air from escaping the back of the vehicle.

questions.question: An empty combination vehicle with stiff suspension springs and strong brakes will have:
questions.explanation: An empty combination vehicle stops more slowly than a loaded one. With less weight, the stiff suspension springs and strong brakes produce lower traction than with a full load.

questions.question: To avoid sudden lane changes, you should:

options.text: Use your horn to encourage other drivers to move out of your lane.
Only drive slower than the posted speed limit.
Watch the road ahead while driving.
Pull off the road and wait when there is high traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the road ahead while driving.
questions.explanation: Sudden lane changes are dangerous when driving a combination vehicle. Look ahead for obstacles that will require a lane change so you can plan ahead.

questions.question: When do rollovers happen?

options.text: When you plan an escape route.

questions.explanation: Rollovers happen when drivers take turns too fast.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?

options.text: The Anti-Lock Braking System will activate.
The service air line will activate.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If it loses pressure, the emergency trailer brakes will activate.

questions.question: How do you test the tractor protection valve?

options.text: Remove the parking brake control knob.
Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
Release air by pressing the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air by pressing the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Test the tractor protection valve by letting the air supply charge fully, turning off the engine, then pressing the brake pedal several times to release air. The valve should move to its emergency position when the pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: What should a driver do to prevent a rollover?
questions.explanation: To prevent rollovers, keep the vehicle's center of gravity low by loading cargo as close to the ground as possible.

questions.question: The service air line is controlled by the foot brake and is attached to the ____ valves.
questions.explanation: The service air line is controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake. It is attached to relay valves, which allow the trailer brakes to be applied quickly.

questions.question: What does the trailer air supply control look like?
questions.explanation: On newer vehicles, the trailer air supply control is an eight-sided red knob. It controls the tractor protection valve.

questions.question: What happens if the emergency air line loses pressure?

options.text: The tractor protection valve will open.

questions.explanation: The emergency air line controls the emergency brakes. If it loses pressure, the emergency trailer brakes will activate.

questions.question: In a sudden turn, which trailer is most likely to turn over?
questions.explanation: When turning, steer gently and smoothly. Making a quick turn while pulling trailers is dangerous and can cause the last trailer to roll over.

questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The trailer service air line is also called the control line or signal line.

questions.question: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve back and forth while backing.

questions.explanation: If you cannot back your trailer in a straight line, back on a curved path toward the driver's side. This gives you the best visibility while backing.
